headline: Record quarterly revenue drives sharp profit growth

kpis.label: Total revenues, net of interest expense

summary_short: Citigroup reported Q2 2026 net income of $5.8 billion, up 45% year-over-year, on revenue of $24.8 billion (+14% y/y) -- its best quarterly revenue in a decade -- with diluted EPS of $3.15 versus $1.96 a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue grew across all five businesses plus Legacy Franchises, led by Equity markets (+45% y/y) and Investment Banking (+44% y/y) within Banking; Services posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue. Net credit losses rose 8% y/y but total provision for credit losses fell 12% y/y on a smaller net ACL build. Operating expenses rose 5% y/y on higher compensation and FX translation. CET1 ratio rose to 12.8% from 12.7% q/q, driven by net income and the Banamex stake-sale impact, partly offset by buybacks and dividends. Citi returned ~$5.0 billion to shareholders via buybacks and dividends this quarter, raised its planned dividend 12%, and launched a new $30 billion share-repurchase authorization.

Citi announced a 12% increase to its planned common dividend and launched a new $30 billion share-repurchase authorization; neither was captured in the event's structured guidance[] array because the release does not bind either to a specific forward fiscal period (a requirement for the guidance schema), so both are noted here and in drivers instead. CET1/SLR q/q bps changes were not disclosed in the release's own comparison columns (blank cells); only the release's own disclosed y/y bps deltas were used for CET1, efficiency ratio, and RoTCE.

drivers.explanation: CEO cited double-digit revenue growth in four of five businesses, record Services revenue, and resilient consumer credit performance despite near-term investment headwinds in U.S. Consumer Cards.

drivers.explanation: Growth in each of the five interconnected businesses and Legacy Franchises, plus FX translation, partly offset by a decline in Corporate/Other.
Higher revenues and a lower provision for credit losses, partially offset by higher operating expenses.
Higher net income combined with a lower diluted share count from common share repurchases.
Y/y decline reflects common share repurchases, dividends and higher risk-weighted assets outweighing net income; q/q the ratio rose on net income and the Banamex stake-sale impact.
Revenue grew faster than operating expenses (14% vs 5% y/y), improving the expense-to-revenue ratio.
Net income and favorable AOCI movements, partly offset by common and preferred dividends and buybacks, which were dilutive to book value per share.
Driven by an increase in Services deposits, consistent with average deposit growth across the firm.
